_about: The agreed problem-language phrasing for every DSAIL agent-facing artifact (TJP-643).
Every MCP tool description, the server instructions, the repo READMEs, the `dsail init`
skill and every page of the docs site quote these strings VERBATIM. Drift across surfaces
is the failure mode; this file is the fix, and services/agent_api/test/test_phrasing.py is
the lint that enforces it. Change a phrase here and every surface changes with it.
lead: Turn a written policy into rules a program can check, and get the same answer every time.

trigger_phrases.policy_to_rules: turn a written policy into rules a program can check
trigger_phrases.rule_that_decided: the rule that decided, with a counterexample
trigger_phrases.unknown_is_an_answer: unknown is an answer, not a guess
trigger_phrases.check_extracted_values: check extracted values against a written policy

avoid.audit: A weak discriminator on two independent measurements (TJP-646): it appears about as often on hard-negative prompts as on positives, and the claude.ai catalog returns ten unrelated results for it. Use it in a sentence, never as a lead or a title.
avoid.compliance: Contested, not open: Vanta already sits on it in the claude.ai catalog. A page may say it; nothing leads with it.
avoid.guardrails: Names a different need (output filtering, jailbreak defence). Use it only on the comparison page, by name.
avoid.policy engine / rules engine: Zero catalog results (TJP-646) so the phrase is open, but it is the by-name vocabulary of OPA and Cedar. Use it on the comparison pages, where an agent arrives with that name, and nowhere as our own description.

tools.dsail_compile: Turn a written policy into rules a program can check.
tools.dsail_check: Check extracted values against a written policy and get the same answer every time, with the rule that decided, with a counterexample when one is violated.
tools.dsail_get_prompt_pack: Get the exact questions to ask a document so the answers can be checked against a written policy.
tools.dsail_save_ruleset: Keep a written policy's rules as a named, immutable revision, so a later check answers exactly as this one did.
tools.dsail_load_ruleset: Show a saved policy ruleset exactly as it was stored.
tools.dsail_list_rulesets: See which written policies already have rules a program can check.
tools.dsail_record_approval: Bind a person's sign-off to the exact rules a program will check.
tools.dsail_get_account_status: Know how much of this credential's allowance is used before a limit interrupts a check.
tools.dsail_issue_api_key: Move a policy check from a chat into production code without rewriting the rules a person already approved.
tools.dsail_unit_library: Find out whether two units convert before a rule compares them, so the check does not answer UNKNOWN forever.
tools.dsail_add_unit_converter: Give a policy check the conversion it needs between two units, with a factor a person supplied.
tools.dsail_review: Show a person the rules a program will check, so they can approve exactly those bytes.
tools.dsail_create_team: Start a team so colleagues share one set of policy rules.
tools.dsail_invite_to_team: Invite a colleague into a team by email address.
tools.dsail_team_members: See who is in a team and who administers it.
tools.dsail_remove_from_team: Take somebody out of a team and cut off the keys they issued for it.
tools.dsail_set_team_role: Let another member administer a team, or stop them administering it.
tools.dsail_list_workspaces: See which teams you work in and which one you are working in now.
tools.dsail_use_workspace: Work in a different team, or in your own workspace.
tools.dsail_copy_ruleset: Put a copy of one of your saved policy rulesets into a team.
